verdict.rationale: Lithic ships an official MCP server, so an AI assistant in Cursor, Claude Code or Copilot can execute live API requests from natural-language prompts. Its own blog walks through creating cards, configuring authorization rules and running transactions this way. The natural-language layer comes from the third-party AI assistant rather than a native Lithic interface, and there is no hands-on or independent corroboration. Missing for 10: a native first-party natural-language interface (e.g., in the dashboard), independent or hands-on verification of operating Lithic by NL commands, and documentation of which operations, guardrails and limits apply to NL-driven actions.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Once connected, your AI assistant can search Lithic documentation, inspect endpoint schemas, generate integration code, and execute live API requests, all from within your editor.
Bring Lithic into Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, and other AI editors — search docs and run live API calls in flow.
Create a virtual card and assign it to a test account... Configure Authorization Rules controlling merchant categories, transaction limits, and velocity... Run transactions against those rules
official MCP server documented at https://docs.lithic.com/docs/mcp
